source: What Word D1 database (days table), definition and synonym questions dated 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-14

items.detail: The warmth of the sun in winter / The sound of wind through trees / A sudden feeling of melancholy / A capacity for sharp perception
items.reveal: Answer: The warmth of the sun in winter. From Latin apricus, 'warmed by the sun'.

items.detail: A place where animals gather / A complaint or grievance / A private retreat for sulking / A kennel or dog enclosure
items.reveal: Answer: A private retreat for sulking. Dickens coined it in Bleak House for a room where Mr Jarndyce could growl in peace.

items.detail: A wish so slight it prompts no action / A habit of deferring decisions / The quality of being velvety to the touch / A gentle evening breeze scented with flowers
items.reveal: Answer: A wish so slight it prompts no action. From Latin velle, to wish: wanting something in theory while doing nothing about it.

items.detail: A secret meeting held at night / An object of little or no value / The smallest possible amount; a trifle / A worthless or contemptible person; a villain
items.reveal: Answer: A worthless or contemptible person; a villain. From Old Norse, it was one of the worst insults in medieval Scandinavia.

items.detail: To remove or erase completely / To make numb or insensitive / To darken or obscure / To confuse with technicalities
items.reveal: Answer: To darken or obscure. From Latin, it literally means 'to cover with clouds'.

items.detail: Insufficiently caffeinated / Quietly resentful of authority / Blissfully unconcerned or carefree / Deliberately vague or evasive
items.reveal: Answer: Blissfully unconcerned or carefree. From French, literally 'not worrying'.

items.detail: Moving with heavy, laboured steps / Honest to the point of rudeness / Aggressively defiant or eager to fight / Stubbornly resistant to change
items.reveal: Answer: Aggressively defiant or eager to fight. From Latin truculentus, 'fierce' or 'savage'.

items.detail: Ornate and decorative / Scattered and unfocused / Melodious and flowing / Sheer and delicate
items.reveal: Answer: Sheer and delicate. From Greek, literally 'showing through', like gauzy curtains.

items.detail: A greenish-blue coating on copper or brass / A climbing plant with trailing vines / The spiral pattern in a snail's shell / The smell of grass after rain
items.reveal: Answer: A greenish-blue coating on copper or brass. From Old French 'vert de Grece', green of Greece. It gives old copper roofs their colour.

items.detail: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something / Reluctant to speak or act / Tending to repeat the same mistakes / Decorated with elaborate ornaments
items.reveal: Answer: Strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something. From Latin redolere, to give off a scent.

items.detail: Relating to ancient scrolls / Excessively animated in speech / Prone to fidgeting / Lacking courage; timid
items.reveal: Answer: Lacking courage; timid. From Latin, literally 'small-souled'.

items.detail: Deliberately awkward / Stubbornly persistent / Quietly defiant / Noisily unruly
items.reveal: Answer: Noisily unruly. From Latin obstrepere, 'to make a loud noise against'.

items.detail: Producing a pleasant, numbing sensation / Tending to induce drowsiness or sleep / Relating to sophisticated or refined taste / Having a soothing or calming voice
items.reveal: Answer: Tending to induce drowsiness or sleep. From Latin sopor (sleep) and facere (to make).

items.detail: Slow-moving and lethargic / Tearful or given to weeping / Lacking in moral strength / Excessively sweet or sentimental
items.reveal: Answer: Tearful or given to weeping. From Latin lacrima, a tear.

items.detail: Pursuing several goals at once / Making things worse by meddling / A long or meandering journey / A formal accusation
items.reveal: Answer: A long or meandering journey. Same root as pilgrim, and the peregrine falcon.

items.detail: Having a strong, unpleasant odour / Prone to sudden bursts of enthusiasm / Relating to ancient trade routes / Excessively flattering or ingratiating
items.reveal: Answer: Excessively flattering or ingratiating. From Latin oleum, oil. Think of Uriah Heep.

items.detail: Ancient or timeworn / Ordinary or everyday / Numbered or sequential / Mysterious or puzzling
items.reveal: Answer: Ordinary or everyday. From Latin quotidianus, daily.

items.detail: Slippery or smooth / Thick or viscous / Extremely cold or icy / Transparent or clear
items.reveal: Answer: Extremely cold or icy. From Latin gelidus, icy cold. Same root as gel and gelatine.

items.detail: Excessively luxurious / Slouching lazily / Disreputable, yet rakishly attractive / Speaking in a secretive whisper
items.reveal: Answer: Disreputable, yet rakishly attractive. From French, meaning 'squinting' or 'shady'.

items.detail: Given to using long words / Walking with a limp / Measuring exactly one and a half units / Having many feet, like a centipede
items.reveal: Answer: Given to using long words. Literally 'a foot and a half long', and itself a fine example.

items.detail: Prone to angry outbursts / Calm and unemotional / Speaking thickly or unclearly / Suffering from a heavy cold
items.reveal: Answer: Calm and unemotional. From the old theory of the four humours, where phlegm made you calm.

items.detail: Scanty or meagre in quantity / Existing outside normal boundaries / Gradually worn away by time / Excessively demanding or particular
items.reveal: Answer: Scanty or meagre in quantity. From Latin exiguus, small or petty.

items.detail: Tediously wordy / Having many layers of meaning / Relating to an early draft / Prone to sudden changes of mood
items.reveal: Answer: Tediously wordy. From Latin prolixus, 'poured forth'.

items.detail: Innocent or naive in character / Quiet and gently sad / Softly bright or glowing, playing lightly over a surface / Moving with a graceful, leaping motion
items.reveal: Answer: Softly bright or glowing, playing lightly over a surface. From Latin lambere, to lick, like flames licking at wood.

items.detail: Impossible to keep steady / Unable to be salvaged / Unhealthy or unwholesome / Not fond of salted foods
items.reveal: Answer: Unhealthy or unwholesome. From Latin, literally 'not healthful'.

items.detail: The quality of being proper or fitting / Nearness in place, time, or relationship / A tendency to make inappropriate remarks / An inherited characteristic or trait
items.reveal: Answer: Nearness in place, time, or relationship. From Latin propinquus, near.

items.detail: Relating to evening or twilight / Glowing with inner light / Vanishing quickly; fleeting / Growing stronger over time
items.reveal: Answer: Vanishing quickly; fleeting. From Latin evanescere, to vanish.

items.detail: Bittersweet and nostalgic / Smooth and honey-sweet in sound / Rich and buttery in texture / Flowing in gentle curves
items.reveal: Answer: Smooth and honey-sweet in sound. Literally 'flowing with honey'.

items.detail: Trembling with uncertainty / Inquisitive and probing / Habitually complaining / Speaking in riddles
items.reveal: Answer: Habitually complaining. From Latin queri, to complain, the same root as quarrel.

items.detail: Active during twilight, at dawn or dusk / Covered in small wrinkles or creases / Making a crackling or rustling sound / Relating to ancient or crumbling structures
items.reveal: Answer: Active during twilight, at dawn or dusk. From Latin crepusculum, twilight. Deer and rabbits are crepuscular.

items.detail: Excessively formal / Deliberately obscure / Previously mentioned / Artificial substitute
items.reveal: Answer: Artificial substitute. Borrowed from German in the First World War, as in ersatz coffee made from acorns.

items.detail: A three-part harmony / A prophecy of doom / A song of lamentation / A morning prayer
items.reveal: Answer: A song of lamentation. From the Greek words for lament and song.

items.detail: Decorated in poor taste / Making harsh, grating sounds / Habitually bad-tempered / Excessively talkative
items.reveal: Answer: Excessively talkative. From Latin garrire, to chatter.

items.detail: Rough to the touch / Stiff and inflexible / Broken into fragments / Full of twists and turns
items.reveal: Answer: Full of twists and turns. From Latin anfractus, a bending.

items.detail: A temporary truce / A moment of perfect timing / A calculated insult / An unexpected, embarrassing mishap
items.reveal: Answer: An unexpected, embarrassing mishap. From French, originally a fencing term for a thrust out of rhythm.

items.detail: A royal decree or proclamation / A philosophical meditation on friendship / A formal apology delivered in public / A bitter verbal attack or denunciation
items.reveal: Answer: A bitter verbal attack or denunciation. Named after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip II of Macedon.

items.detail: To whisper conspiratorially / To argue persuasively / To move with exaggerated grace / To make harsh, discordant sounds
items.reveal: Answer: To make harsh, discordant sounds. Originally the yowling of cats in heat.

items.detail: Filtering through fine cloth / Flattery intended to deceive / Light, bantering talk / A state of bewilderment
items.reveal: Answer: Light, bantering talk. From French persifler, to banter.

items.detail: Someone newly rich who lacks refinement / A small ornamental French garden / A minor legal offence / A delicate cream-filled pastry
items.reveal: Answer: Someone newly rich who lacks refinement. From French, literally 'arrived'. Always said by old money about new.

items.detail: A love potion / The soft roof of the mouth / A flourish in calligraphy / The groove between nose and upper lip
items.reveal: Answer: The groove between nose and upper lip. From Greek philtron, a love charm.

items.detail: Books printed before 1501 / The innermost chambers of a temple / Ancient prophecies in symbols / Sleeping quarters in monasteries
items.reveal: Answer: Books printed before 1501. From Latin 'in cunabulis', in the cradle: books from printing's infancy.

items.detail: The embezzlement of public funds / Examining something in minute detail / A distinctive way of walking / Hoarding small, worthless objects
items.reveal: Answer: The embezzlement of public funds. It shares a root with peculiar, which once meant privately owned.

items.detail: Easily broken or fragile / Capable of being shaped or moulded / Having a pleasant fragrance / Able to be divided into fractions
items.reveal: Answer: Easily broken or fragile. From Latin frangere, to break, like fracture and fragment.

items.detail: Slightly disreputable in an appealing way / Relating to a ship's upper rigging / Rough and unfinished in texture / Fond of raffles
items.reveal: Answer: Slightly disreputable in an appealing way. From riff-raff. Raffish people are rogues, not villains.

items.detail: A trap for small rodents / A cloth hung over a throne / A secret hoarder of wealth / A petty, tyrannical local ruler
items.reveal: Answer: A petty, tyrannical local ruler. Satraps were provincial governors in the ancient Persian Empire.

items.detail: To speak in a whisper or undertone / To crumble or decay gradually / To move with hesitant, shuffling steps / To make repeated crackling or popping sounds
items.reveal: Answer: To make repeated crackling or popping sounds. From Latin crepitare, to crackle. Fires and creaky knees both crepitate.

items.detail: Prone to dramatic gestures / Extremely wicked or villainous / Relating to flags or banners / Excessively flattering
items.reveal: Answer: Extremely wicked or villainous. From Latin flagitium, a shameful act.

items.detail: Pleasantly warm / Cautiously hesitant / Dark and gloomy / Thin and delicate
items.reveal: Answer: Dark and gloomy. From Latin tenebrae, darkness.

items.detail: Scholarly precision / Excessive ornamentation / Physical beauty / Moral corruption
items.reveal: Answer: Physical beauty. From Latin pulchritudo, beauty. An ungainly word for a lovely thing.

items.detail: Causing disgust or irritation; repellent / Able to grow back after being cut / Relating to beards or facial hair / Speaking in a rough, rasping voice
items.reveal: Answer: Causing disgust or irritation; repellent. It sounds like it should involve beards, but it means off-putting.

items.detail: A midnight gathering under a full moon / The sadness that follows great joy / A period of unrestrained revelry / A winter solstice ceremony
items.reveal: Answer: A period of unrestrained revelry. From the Roman winter festival, when social rules were turned upside down.

items.detail: A devotee of formal debate / A person devoted to luxury and pleasure / A collector of rare gemstones / A scholar of ancient texts
items.reveal: Answer: A person devoted to luxury and pleasure. From Sybaris, an ancient Greek city famed for luxurious living.

items.detail: A build-up of crusty deposits / The harmful breaking out of something again after dormancy / The gradual healing of a wound / A revival of crude customs
items.reveal: Answer: The harmful breaking out of something again after dormancy. From Latin, 'to become raw again', like a wound reopening.

items.detail: Prone to sudden fits of weeping / Relating to February or midwinter coldness / Feverish or marked by intense nervous energy / Fragile and easily broken into fibres
items.reveal: Answer: Feverish or marked by intense nervous energy. From Latin febris, fever.

items.detail: Skilled in household management / Suspicious of marriage itself / Excessively devoted to one's wife / Fond of luxury and comfort
items.reveal: Answer: Excessively devoted to one's wife. From Latin uxor, wife. Always used with gentle mockery.
